body_text:
An *explicit definition* introduces a new symbol or syntactic
shorthand by equating it with an expression formed entirely
from previously established concepts. A legitimate definition
must satisfy Stanisław Leśniewski's dual criteria of
*eliminability* (any occurrence of the new symbol can be
systematically replaced by its definiens) and *non-creativity*
(the definition cannot enable the proof of any new theorem in
the original vocabulary).

An *implicit definition* or axiomatic specification
characterizes an entity by the system of relations it satisfies
with other objects. Implicit definitions are mathematically
permissible only when existence and uniqueness have been
rigorously established, ensuring that the defined entity is
neither impossible nor ambiguous.
